subject: Hosted API capacity uplift & billing lanes for Horizon Retail
messages:
From: Ben Turner <ben.turner@horizonretail.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity — potential uplift

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We've been reviewing March–May usage and it looks like our peak windows are growing faster than we expected. At our current hosted plan, we're hitting burst throttles on two weekdays and are seeing queueing which impacts our user-facing sync jobs.

Quick snapshot attached (usage_report_Mar-May.csv). High level ask: we're interested in increasing our monthly committed throughput to avoid throttles and reduce per-token variability — ideally starting next billing cycle.

Questions:
- What are the practical commit bands you support for hosted customers?
- Can we get predictable rate limits for our production route during business hours?
- Any options around an initial ramp (credit or burst cushion) while we shift traffic?

We're aiming to finalize something by end of month. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Ben
Ben Turner
VP Engineering, Horizon Retail
ben.turner@horizonretail.com
+1 415 555 0199

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Turner <ben.turner@horizonretail.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity — potential uplift

Thanks Ben — appreciate the usage snapshot. High level, we can do two practical paths depending on how aggressive you want the economics and term to be:

Option A (recommended for immediate relief)
- Commit uplift to 1.8x current monthly units, 12-month term
- New daytime rate band for your production route (M–F 07:00–22:00 local): reduced per-1k token price compared to current hosted tier
- One-time "ramp credit" equal to 10% of first invoice to help absorb re-routing/testing costs
- Start date: 2027-06-01 (billing aligned)

Option B (more flexibility, shorter term)
- Commit uplift to 1.4x, 6-month term, slightly higher per-token price than A
- Include 72 hours/month burst credits for scheduled tests

I've attached a draft proposal that lays out pricing, SLOs (latency targets for the production route), and rollback/fallback policies: Horizon_Commit_Proposal_v2.pdf.

If Option A looks right, I'll loop in finance for billing window and get a DocuSign to route. If you want a hybrid (start at 1.4x for 60 days then ramp to 1.8x), we can model that too.

Proposed next steps:
1) You flag preferred option (A/B/hybrid)
2) I'll send the finalized proposal and DocuSign for signature
3) We execute a 7–14 day pre-cutover validation with our infra team + your SREs
--
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0112

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Internal: Horizon uplift — pricing & billing lane details

Aditya / Priyom / Rachel — quick internal thread before I send the signed-up plan to Ben.

Ben is leaning toward Option A but asked if we can soften the first-month impact. I'm proposing: 1.8x commit, 12-month term, but give a 10% credit on the first invoice and allow a 30-day ramp window where they won't be charged for overage beyond the committed lane while they shift traffic.

Questions for finance/solutions:
- Rachel: can we structure the 10% as an invoice credit (vs. retroactive rebate) and keep the billing cycle aligned to 1 Jun start?
- Aditya: ops needs the ramp window documented in the runbook — I assume we can add a FIFO preemption policy for their production route during the 30-day ramp so other customers' SLAs are preserved.
- Priyom: approve discount comp (target TCV impact ~ -8% YoY vs naive 1.8x price).

I'll aim to send a revised DocuSign by Thu if we all agree.

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Turner <ben.turner@horizonretail.com>, Horizon Retail Procurement <procurement@horizonretail.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:30:00 -04:00
Subject: Finalized: 1.8x capacity uplift & billing lanes — next steps

Ben / team — thanks for the quick turn. Per our call this morning, we've finalized the path below and attached the proposed contract in DocuSign: https://docusign.com/link/placeholder/hzn-commit-2027

Agreed commercial summary:
- Commit uplift: 1.8x current monthly units (starts 2027-06-01)
- Term: 12 months
- Ramp support: 30-day ramp window post-cutover where overages beyond committed lane are waived
- One-time ramp credit: 10% of month 1 invoice applied as an invoice credit on first billing statement
- Daytime production route rate band: reduced per-1k token price (documented in attached PDF)

Operational notes:
- We'll schedule a joint runbook review and cutover test between 2027-05-25 and 2027-05-31. Aditya / ops will own the validation checklist.
- Priyom will confirm the escalation contact list and SLOs to include in the DocuSign exhibit.
- Rachel: please confirm billing window and invoice credit semantics before I send the DocuSign envelope.

Ben, when you sign the DocuSign I'll have our implementation team schedule the validation slots and pre-provision the increased lanes. Let me know if you want the hybrid ramp (1.4x then 1.8x) modeled — otherwise I'll proceed with this final.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
